developers.title: Developers — automate cloud file transfers
developers.description: Move files between clouds with a typed HTTP API, a CLI, webhooks, and runners you can host yourself.
developers.heroHeadline: Automate cloud file transfers with an API, CLI, webhooks, and runners.
developers.heroSubheading: For agencies moving client assets, SaaS teams importing or exporting customer files, and internal tools that move bytes between provider APIs without writing the glue.
developers.audienceLabel: Built for agencies, SaaS engineering teams, platform groups, and internal tooling.
developers.apiBody: Create a job with a source, a destination, a runner choice, and an optional schedule. The control plane validates, picks a runner, and emits progress events.
developers.apiCaption: Sketch — final shape will land with the v1 API.
developers.cliTitle: A CLI for scripts and CI
developers.cliBody: Same jobs, driven from a terminal or a CI runner. Useful for one-shot migrations and for backups owned by a script you can read in a code review.
developers.cliCaption: Planned. Behavior mirrors the API one-to-one.
developers.runnersTitle: Pick the runner that fits the job
developers.runnersBody: Same API. Three different data paths. Choose per job, not per account.

runnerCloud.title: Cloud Runner
runnerCloud.desc: Hosted runners for scheduled jobs and large migrations. No infrastructure on your side.

runnerBrowser.title: Browser Runner
runnerBrowser.desc: For ad-hoc transfers from a tab. The data path stays in the user's browser; no long-lived tokens.

runnerPrivate.title: Private Runner
runnerPrivate.desc: Self-host the runner binary in your VPC, on-prem, or on a NAS. Outbound-only connection to the control plane.

developers.webhooksTitle: Webhooks for the events you care about
developers.webhooksBody: Subscribe to job lifecycle events and stream them into your queue, your dashboard, or your audit log. Payloads will be HMAC-signed.
developers.noSdkBody: We will not ship an official SDK before the API is stable. The OpenAPI spec will be public, so you can generate a typed client in any language you already use.
developers.surveyTitle: Which developer surface matters most to you?
developers.surveyBody: Pick the one you would reach for first. It helps us decide what ships first.
developers.surveyHint: Local signal only — your pick is not sent anywhere. Use the waitlist below to share more.

faq.a: We are not committing to a date. The API will land alongside the first paid Cloud Runner tier. The waitlist is the right way to be first in line for early access.

faq.q: Will there be a free tier for developers?
faq.a: The Browser Runner stays free, and the Private Runner is free for the runner itself. Cloud Runner usage is what we plan to bill for.

faq.q: Do you handle OAuth on behalf of my users?
faq.a: Yes. The control plane handles provider OAuth so transfers can run unattended. Users connect their accounts through Syncologic, not through your app.

faq.q: Can I run jobs entirely on my own infrastructure?
faq.a: Yes. The Private Runner runs in your VPC, on a NAS, or on a developer machine. The control plane never touches your file bytes.
Webhook payloads will be HMAC-signed with a per-workspace secret you control. Replay protection and timestamp tolerance follow the same conventions you would expect from Stripe or Linear.
